subject: feat: implement the full roadmap — provider matrix, observability, governance, workflows, and scale (#19)
branch triage: retire all 8 stale local codex/* branches
decision: Delete all 8 local codex/* branches without opening PRs; GitHub main (87ff2c0, v2.4.1) already contains every salvageable change.
why: Measured each branch with two-dot diff against github/main tip rather than three-dot (which compares against the merge-base and misleadingly renders main's newer work as branch additions). Every branch is strictly behind main: codex/secrets-sync-fabric-boundary is 0 ahead/14 behind (fully merged); preserve-local-main-release-work, cd-rerun-idempotent, ci-cache-polish and final-alignment are patch-identical upstream per git cherry '-' and shipped as merged PRs #14/#11/#10; cd-publish-fix and stabilization-wip show git cherry '+' only because they were squash-merged (PRs #12 and #8) so SHAs cannot match — their content is superseded, e.g. main's tools/check_python_dist.py is 108 lines including tag validation from PR #15 versus the branch's 76, and main already completed the cmd/secretsync to cmd/secrets-sync rename that the branch would revert; go-1.26.5-runtime-fix differs from main tip in only .release-please-manifest.json and CHANGELOG.md, where main is ahead by the release-please 2.4.1 commit. Merging any branch would regress main, so no PR is warranted.

subject: branch triage re-verification: per-file supersession proof against github/main
decision: Re-verified all 8 retired branches against github/main explicitly (never --remotes or origin/*, which resolve to Gitea and can falsely report a branch as contained). Confirm the retirement of all 8, including codex/secrets-sync-stabilization-wip whose 40 branch-unique files are a deliberately superseded architecture rather than lost work.
why: Commit-count heuristics are unreliable across squash merges, so supersession was proven per file: for every file touched by each branch's unique commits, the branch blob either matches main's blob or main modified that file later. Six branches came back fully superseded (identical or main_newer for every file) and codex/secrets-sync-fabric-boundary is a strict ancestor of main. codex/secrets-sync-stabilization-wip was the one real divergence: 40 files where main is not newer, about 24 absent from main entirely. Investigated rather than assumed. Two distinct causes, both intentional. First, cmd/secretsync/, scripts/break-fork.sh, docs/ARCHITECTURE_GAP_ANALYSIS.md and several examples were deliberately deleted on main by 19730c8 'feat: retire Python bridge from secrets-sync' (2026-06-26), which predates the branch tip (2026-06-27) but is itself already merged; restoring them would revive the retired bridge. Second, the secrets-sync-operator and secrets-sync-events Helm subcharts plus api/v1alpha1 never existed on main and encode a competing CRD design: group secrets-sync.extendeddata.dev with kind SecretSync, the legacy ExtendedData-era identity. Main instead ships group secrets-sync.jbcom.dev with kind CredentialSynchronization, a flat chart with controller-deployment/rbac/serviceaccount templates, deploy/crds/secrets-sync.jbcom.dev_credentialsynchronizations.yaml, and a 470-line pkg/kubernetes/controller.go with tests, built out by PR #19 in July after the branch was abandoned. Verified main's implementation is complete and not a stub: helm lint passes, helm_chart_test.go and kubernetes_crd_test.go pass, no TODO or FIXME markers. Merging the branch would resurrect a dead CRD group and fork the operator surface, so retiring it is the correct call, not a deferral.
resolves: re-triage against github/main per corrected method

subject: policy patterns become whole-name matches (behavior change)
decision: Anchor policy source/target patterns at compile time with ^(?:...)$ instead of treating them as substring searches, and migrate the shipped docs and tests to the prefix form prod-.* rather than ^prod-.
why: regexp.MatchString is a substring search, so a deny rule for prod also denied nonprod and an allow rule for vault-prod was satisfied by evil-vault-prod-x. These rules decide where credentials may be written, so a pattern matching more names than it reads is a privilege-escalation path, and silent over-matching in a security control is worse than a migration. The non-capturing group matters: without it, anchoring staging|prod would bind ^ to the first branch and $ to the last, leaving the middle branches unanchored. This breaks patterns that relied on prefix semantics, which is why docs/USAGE.md, policy_test.go and sync_backend_test.go were updated in the same commit and the whole-name rule is now documented. Chose anchoring over adding an opt-in strict mode because a security default that must be opted into is not a default.
overrides: policy patterns were previously unanchored substring matches

subject: diff redaction moves into the formatter
decision: Redact secret values inside FormatDiffWithOptions on a copy, rather than leaving each caller to strip them after formatting.
why: Only the side-by-side formatter honored the showValues flag, so JSON output serialized CurrentValues and DesiredValues verbatim. The CLI compensated by stripping after the call; the serverless adapter did not, and its default format is JSON, so Lambda and Azure Function responses returned plaintext secrets into HTTP bodies and cloud logs. Per-caller stripping is the wrong shape for an invariant this important because it fails open by omission: any new format or entry point leaks until someone remembers. Redacting at the single chokepoint every caller already passes through makes forgetting impossible. The copy is deliberate rather than incidental: callers reuse the diff for audit records and returned results, so an in-place strip would blank data those consumers legitimately hold, which is why RedactChangeValues exists separately for the caller-owned envelope.
resolves: critical plaintext secret leak via serverless JSON diff

subject: fail closed where a requested protection cannot be provided
decision: Fail the target when rollback is enabled but the pre-sync snapshot fails, and treat a time window whose timezone cannot be loaded as not satisfied, instead of continuing in both cases.
why: Both previously failed open while logging a warning. In each the operator had explicitly asked for the protection: rollback.enabled true, or a named timezone on a maintenance window. Proceeding anyway left the safety net silently absent, and its absence would only surface during the failure it was meant to cover. The timezone case is a realistic deployment difference rather than a theoretical one, since Validate checks the zone at config load and a container image without tzdata fails only at runtime, evaluating an America/New_York window in UTC and opening it hours off. For a tool that writes credentials, refusing to act is the safe direction.
resolves: time window evaluated in the wrong zone

subject: dynamic target discovery wired into construction
decision: Call expansion during pipeline construction after the AWS execution context exists, rebuild the dependency graph, and turn two previously-empty outcomes into hard errors.
why: ExpandDynamicTargets had zero callers, so the entire discovery path including pkg/discovery/identitycenter was unreachable, which is what the 4 percent coverage figure actually measured. Validate accepts a config with no static targets when dynamic_targets is set and four docs pages describe the feature, so following the documentation produced a pipeline that synced nothing and reported success. Chose to wire the feature up rather than reject dynamic_targets in Validate and strip the docs, because the discovery implementation is complete and tested and only the call site was missing. Expansion has to run after the AWS context is built and before the graph is used, so construction is the only correct point. Requesting dynamic targets without a usable AWS context, and discovery resolving to zero targets, now fail loudly rather than producing an empty run.
resolves: documented dynamic-targets feature was a silent no-op
